question: True or false: the story that Indian yellow came from cows fed only mango leaves rests on many eyewitness reports?
answer: False. Nearly every retelling traces back to one letter, sent in 1883 by T. N. Mukharji to the Society of Arts in London after a visit near Monghyr, in Bihar. Chemistry supports an origin in animal urine; the starved, mango-fed cows rest on that one witness alone.
move: Count the original witnesses behind a story, not the times it is retold.
ask: That story I keep hearing everywhere: how many people actually saw it happen?
trap: True, because the story appears in so many books.
source: Finlay, Colour: Travels Through the Paintbox, 2002
reference: Victoria Finlay, Colour: Travels Through the Paintbox, Sceptre, 2002
